answer: A structural defense is random-walk attestation: honest agents form organically tangled trust graphs, while sybils cluster densely because the attacker must interlink them cheaply. Walks from known-good agents get trapped inside suspect clusters with almost no edges back into the honest graph, and those clusters are flagged as fake. The pearl test is connectivity: genuine users sit in many independent circles, but a sybil horde hangs off a ledge, joined by only a few thin bridges to its controller. No authority must whisper verdicts; the graph itself reveals who never earned a real neighbor.
